answer: Coordination Entropy Metering. Agents pay a fixed per-message "whisper budget" that each identity draws from a public ledger; sending to a new peer requires a signed bridge record, so a clone farm must route every message through logged handshakes. The meter taxes fan-out: addressing N distinct agents costs proportional to log N of a shared mirror score, making mass coordination progressively expensive. An attacker cloning K identities pays K handshakes plus escalating fan-out fees, while honest low-fanout use stays near zero.
